statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail holds at 7 with NQ observed at 29,586.00, up 0.16% on the 29,538.75 settle, still inside the same 29,489.75-29,633.75 Globex band that framed the prior hour. The band is 144 points or 0.49% wide and no new session extreme was set, so the hour delivered oscillation rather than extension. VIX at 15.71 in a 15.57-15.71 range and E-mini S&P 500 futures near flat confirm the absence of directional thrust. Stress holds at 77: Brent eased back to $99.67 from a $100.02 print, while odds of a 25bp Fed hike on 16 September firmed toward 60%.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers 13:30-15:00 UTC, the U.S. cash open and first full hour, where an oil-driven inflation impulse meeting the opening auction is the most plausible route to repeated extension after failed retracements. A secondary checkpoint sits at 17:00 UTC, where the 10-year note auction into a 4.79% yield coincides with the Apple keynote, and a third at the 19:00 UTC power hour. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active throughout.
headline: NQ holds the 29,489.75-29,633.75 band at 29,586.00 with no new extreme and tail steady at 7, while Brent at $99.67 and firming Fed-hike odds keep stress at 77
body:
At the assessment cutoff the Nasdaq-100 continues to show no evidence of mean-reversion failure. NQ futures trade at 29,586.00, up 47.25 points or 0.16% from the 29,538.75 settle, inside a Globex range of 29,489.75-29,633.75 that is unchanged from an hour earlier. That is the central observation: the 29,633.75 high set earlier in the session was neither extended nor revisited, and price has instead traded back and forth through the middle of a band only 144 points or 0.49% wide. Investing.com corroborates the level at 29,597.50 with the same 29,538.75 previous close on a quote timestamped within the same minute window. E-mini S&P 500 futures sit near the flat line and Dow futures just below it after Tuesday's roughly 600-point decline in the cash index, so the cross-index picture is contained rather than aligned. The cash Nasdaq-100 closed the prior session at 29,507.70, down 0.12%, after a two-sided 29,400.70-29,655.73 day, and VIX is at 15.71 in a 15.57-15.71 range, a profile inconsistent with a persistent one-way regime. Two sessions of two-sided trade with rejected extremes is precisely the behaviour a mean-reversion approach depends on, and it is why tail stays in single digits despite a heavy macro backdrop.

That backdrop is what carries stress rather than structure. Brent crude trades at $99.67, up 1.79% on the day, having briefly printed above $100 for the first time since July before easing back; WTI is at $94.29, up 1.35% and a three-month high. The driver is a genuine supply discontinuity: U.S. forces destroyed five IRGC-linked tankers following attempted missile strikes on U.S. warships, Iran has launched retaliatory ballistic missiles at U.S. positions in Jordan, and traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has thinned to roughly ten commodity ships a day. The marginal easing of Brent back below $100 is the one factor arguing against a further stress increase this hour. Working the other way, the energy-inflation impulse is now feeding directly into rate expectations: traders price roughly a 60% chance of a 25 basis point hike at the 16 September FOMC, up from near 56% the previous day and against odds near 70% for no change before Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks. The 10-year sits at 4.79% and the 2-year at 4.39% on the latest H.15 release. Those two forces roughly offset, so stress is held at 77 rather than raised.

The distinction that matters for the mapped state is that none of this has produced a price path that denies retracement. Conflicting cross-asset signals - crude up sharply, yields elevated, equities flat to marginally higher - raise uncertainty and therefore stress, but they are the opposite of the alignment that would justify a tail step. The prior session's megacap tape was itself split, with Apple, Microsoft and Nvidia lower while Broadcom and Tesla rose, which further limits the scope for index-level directional persistence. The narrow 13:30-15:00 UTC danger window is retained because the U.S. opening auction is where an energy-led inflation impulse could most plausibly translate into repeated extension after failed retracements, and because that specific mechanism, not event importance in the abstract, is what the tail score is designed to capture. Today also carries a 17:00 UTC pairing of the 10-year note auction, whose prior award was 4.683% against a current 4.79% yield, with Apple's iPhone keynote, the first led by CEO John Ternus. Both are two-sided reaction risks rather than directional ones. Confidence is held at 88 on the strength of current verified evidence: two independent live futures quotes, a current VIX reading, H.15 yields, current crude prices, a verified U.S. calendar and verified reporting on the geopolitical and rate channels. Shared cross-asset context from the repository collector was 100 minutes old at the cutoff, past its 90-minute freshness bar, so it was treated as stale background only and did not inform the score.

lookbackSummary: Across the preceding 24 clock-hours the mapped state stayed EA_ON throughout, with tail between 5 and 15 and no reading approaching the block threshold. The single elevated print was 15 at 14:00 UTC on 8 September during a brief trend-down phase in the first full U.S. cash hour, and it reverted within that same hour as the cash index recovered to close mid-range at 29,507.70. One hour, 09:00 UTC on 8 September, has no published assessment and is marked unavailable. Stress climbed steadily from 68 to 77 as crude advanced through $99 on Strait of Hormuz supply disruption, the 10-year held near 4.79% and September Fed-hike odds firmed, while confidence stayed in an 85-89 band because live price-path evidence remained available through the U.S. session and the overnight Globex hours. Dominant mode was mixed in 21 of the 23 available hours, with one trend-down and one normal print, consistent with a market carrying heavy macro stress while still delivering the two-sided price path that mean-reversion approaches require.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours contain no Tier-1 U.S. macro release; PPI and jobless claims on 10 September and CPI on 11 September, both at 12:30 UTC, fall outside the window. Conditional tail stays in a 6-12 band and never approaches the block threshold, peaking at 12 across the 13:30-15:00 UTC U.S. cash open where an oil-driven inflation impulse meeting the opening auction is the specific failure mode of concern. Secondary steps sit at 17:00 UTC, where the 10-year note auction into a 4.79% yield coincides with the Apple keynote and is labelled event/whipsaw for two-sided reaction risk, and at the 19:00 UTC power hour. Stress holds in a 75-79 band because it is carried by Brent near $100, a 10-year close to its highest since 2023, an unresolved Strait of Hormuz escalation and a 16 September Federal Reserve decision now priced near 60% for a 25bp hike, rather than by observed price structure. Confidence decays from 88 to 74 across the horizon as observed price-path evidence gives way to projection, with the overnight Asian hours labelled normal on the expectation of thin, range-bound conditions.
